title: From Vertical Load to Sacral Unloading: The Role of Constraint-Modulated Poisson Ratios in Pelvic Floor Load Transfer
content: Female pelvic-floor support is a coupled biomechanical system involving the vagina, uterus, pelvic connective tissues, ligaments, levator ani, and pelvic boundaries. Published finite-element studies demonstrate that changes in intra-abdominal pressure (IAP), tissue impairment, and pelvic geometry alter stress and displacement patterns. This study proposes a constraint-modulated load-transfer framework in which pressure-induced deformation is redistributed through the interconnected pelvic support structures toward posterior pelvic boundaries. Within this framework, three metrics are defined: geometric Poisson’s ratio (νg), structural Poisson’s ratio (νs), and composite Poisson’s ratio (νc). The proposed composite Poisson’s ratio (νc) is introduced as a candidate system-level outcome measure rather than an established clinical or validated numerical biomarker. No new experimental or original finite-element simulation outputs are generated in this work; all interpretations draw upon previously-published literature. This manuscript integrates published biomechanical evidence with a proposed finite element (FE) validation protocol without claiming unsupported original numerical stress or displacement results.
